messages:
Kenton H.: hey team, Kenton here starting today. quick kube question: `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows `kind-cluster`. I need read on `staging` and a personal ns `kenton-onboard` to test ingress examples. who should I raise a ticket with and what exact info should I include? :wave:

Rae (DevEx): welcome Kenton! :tada: open an eng-infra ticket and include your corporate email, manager, which namespaces and whether you need read or write. paste `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` so infra can merge your kubeconfig. Also mention if you need networkpolicy or ingress tweaks for your onboarding tests.

Kenton H.: pasted flattened kubeconfig below (very small):
```
apiVersion: v1
clusters: []
contexts: []
current-context: kind-cluster
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: kind-user
```

I created ticket INF-1102 and cc'd @sophie_p.

onboard-bot: ticket INF-1102 created and assigned to eng-infra. https://tickets.redwood/INF-1102

Marta (Eng-Infra): hi Kenton  process note: we map SSO groups to k8s roles. For onboarding we typically create a namespace `kenton-onboard` and bind `edit` role. For staging read we add you to `redwood-staging-read`. If your ingress tests need a LoadBalancer/ingress tweak say so. ETA ~8m, I'll post when done.

Marta (Eng-Infra): applied namespace and bindings. Please verify these commands:
```
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace=kenton-onboard
kubectl auth can-i list services --namespace=staging
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=kenton-onboard
```

Kenton H.: ran checks  contexts now show `redwood-staging` and `kenton-onboard`; `auth can-i` returned yes for get pods in my ns and yes for list services in staging. I deployed a tiny nginx in `kenton-onboard` and it came up. thanks! :+1:

Rae (DevEx): great! couple of onboarding tips: 1) switch contexts with `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` when you need staging, 2) to avoid merging problems run `kubectl config view --flatten > ~/.kube/config && chmod 600 ~/.kube/config`, 3) if you need staging write access for a short experiment request temporary elevation with an expiry (we default to 48h).

Marta (Eng-Infra): security reminder: onboarding namespaces get a default NetworkPolicy blocking ingress from other namespaces. If your tests require cross-namespace traffic or external LB, add that detail to the ticket and we'll scope it.

Kenton H.: noted, thanks everyone for the quick help and the tips. I'll close INF-1102 after I finish my demo. :raised_hands:
